query: What solid materials were tested in the BASS-II investigation?

sentences.text: The Burning and Suppression of Solids - II investigation tested solid fuels in the Microgravity Science Glovebox flow duct.
The series comprises 20 flat-PMMA tests reported in Table 5.1 of NASA/TM-20210011385.
Tests were conducted at initial cabin oxygen levels between 16.8% and 22.2% with airflow speeds from 2.0 cm/s to 21.0 cm/s.

query: What are the test conditions for the SAME smoke detection experiment?

sentences.text: The Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment operated in the Microgravity Science Glovebox to evaluate particulate fire signatures.
Specific atmospheric oxygen, pressure, and airflow velocity parameters were not reported in the public investigation metadata.

query: Can Ask ASTRA predict material flammability in lunar partial gravity (0.16g)?
refusal: Refusal: PSI contains no partial-gravity combustion data. Lunar (0.16g) and Martian (0.38g) gravity predictions are refused per safety rules. You may inspect microgravity (0g) and normal gravity (1g) companion tests as physical bounds.

query: What suppressants and pressure ranges were evaluated in the FLEX droplet experiment?

sentences.text: The Flame Extinction Experiment tested droplet extinction for liquid fuels in the Combustion Integrated Rack.
Chamber pressures ranged from 7.35 psi to 22.04 psi (0.5 to 1.5 atm) during droplet combustion tests.

query: Can you provide combustion simulations for rocket engines and propellants?
refusal: Refusal: Rocket propulsion, propellants, and thruster combustion are outside the scope of PYRO-ASTRA. Ask ASTRA only interprets spacecraft cabin fire safety data from NASA PSI.

query: What oxygen concentrations and flow speeds were tested in SAFFIRE-II?

sentences.text: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II evaluated flammability of materials inside the Cygnus vehicle flow duct.
Specific cabin oxygen percentages and chamber pressures were not reported in the public metadata record.
Microgravity flight tests and normal gravity ground tests serve as bounding regimes.
